sentenceSets.sentence: The two rival firms agreed to amalgamate, combining their resources to compete in a tougher market.

answerChoices.reasoning: Merge is a very close synonym in business contexts but emphasizes one entity absorbing another; amalgamate implies a more thorough blending into a new unified entity.
Consolidate means to combine into a stronger whole, often through reduction; it is close but focuses on strengthening and streamlining rather than the fusion into a new combined entity.
Integrate means to bring parts together into a whole; it is close but can describe incorporating one part into another rather than the mutual blending implied by amalgamate.
Collaborate means to work together; firms that collaborate remain separate entities, whereas amalgamate means they become one—an important structural distinction.
Partner means to form an alliance while remaining independent; it describes a relationship short of the full blending that amalgamate requires.
Coordinate means to organize joint action; it does not imply forming a single entity and lacks the sense of combining resources into one organization.
Align means to bring into agreement or cooperation; it describes moving in the same direction while remaining distinct, not the creation of a unified entity.
Compete is the opposite of what the firms want to do with each other; they amalgamate precisely to compete more effectively against third parties.
Dissolve means to break up and cease to exist; it is the opposite of combining resources to build a stronger market presence.
Fragment means to break into pieces—the opposite of bringing two firms together into a unified entity.
Divest means to sell off assets or subsidiaries—the opposite of combining resources through merger.

sentenceSets.sentence: The historian described how the three warring clans eventually chose to amalgamate rather than continue a war of mutual destruction.

answerChoices.reasoning: Unite is very close in meaning but is broader and more neutral; amalgamate specifically implies the blending of previously distinct groups into something new rather than simply standing together.
Federate means to join in a federation while preserving some independence; amalgamate implies a more thorough merger where the distinct identities dissolve into one.
Reconcile means to restore friendly relations; it describes ending hostility without necessarily merging into a single entity.
Coalesce means to come together to form one mass; it is very close to amalgamate but tends to describe a more gradual, organic process, while amalgamate can be a deliberate formal act.
Assimilate means to absorb into a dominant culture or group; it implies one side dominating rather than the mutual blending that amalgamate suggests for equally matched clans.
Negotiate means to discuss and reach an agreement; the clans may have negotiated before amalgamating, but negotiate describes the process, not the outcome of combining.
Subjugate means to bring under control by force; it implies conquest rather than the voluntary mutual merging that amalgamate describes.
Capitulate means to surrender; it implies one side giving up rather than two sides voluntarily combining into one.
Fracture means to break or split—the opposite of the clans coming together into a single entity.
Exterminate means to destroy entirely—the very outcome the clans were trying to avoid by amalgamating.
Scatter means to spread widely in different directions—the opposite of converging into a unified group.

sentenceSets.sentence: The software engineer proposed a script to amalgamate data from three separate databases into a single, searchable repository.

answerChoices.reasoning: Aggregate means to collect into a mass or total; it is very close but emphasizes summing or counting rather than the thorough blending into a unified structure that amalgamate implies.
Compile means to collect and assemble from sources; it is close but suggests gathering without the thorough fusion into one coherent structure that amalgamate conveys.
Synchronize means to make systems consistent and coordinated; it preserves separate databases while keeping them aligned rather than merging them into one.
Migrate means to move data from one system to another; it describes movement but not the fusion of multiple sources into one new repository.
Extract means to pull data out; it describes a step in the process but not the act of combining multiple sources into one.
Normalize means to standardize data formats; it is a preparatory step for combining databases but does not itself mean to fuse them.
Duplicate means to copy exactly; it involves multiplication rather than the reduction of three sources to one combined repository.
Index means to organize into a systematic list for searching; a repository might be indexed after amalgamating data, but indexing does not itself mean combining sources.
Partition means to divide into separate sections—the opposite of combining three databases into one.
Corrupt means to introduce errors or damage data—the opposite of building a clean, unified repository.
Delete means to remove data entirely—clearly the opposite of preserving and combining data from three sources.
